transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Samir Patel, Nora Liu (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Marcus Holt, Priya Singh, Ibrahim Khan, Tasha Reed, Jordan (MatrixPay)
Links shared: 1) mini-benchmark.csv (Redwood), 2) incident-timeline.md (MatrixPay doc link noted), 3) security-checklist.pdf

Summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
Short post-incident bridge to review yesterday's 15:10 outage where long-tail latency spiked across the payments validation path. Discussed KV-cache miss amplification, batching backpressure, and fallback policy gaps. Agreed on canary, telemetry export, and security checklist follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Avery Chen: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for jumping on. I see most folks are here. Quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Lena Ortiz: Lena here — VP of Engineering at MatrixPay.
[00:00:14] Marcus Holt: Marcus, SRE. We had the logs open in the incident doc.
[00:00:17] Priya Singh: Priya from security.
[00:00:18] Ibrahim Khan: Ibrahim, platform.
[00:00:20] Tasha Reed: Tasha product.
[00:00:22] Jordan: Jordan, oncall.
[00:00:23] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood infra team, thanks.
[00:00:25] Nora Liu: Nora, CSM.

[00:01:10] Avery Chen: Okay quick objective: surface root causes from your side, share what we saw in our runtime and then align on mitigations + next steps. Marcus, do you want to kick off with a short timeline?
[00:01:25] Marcus Holt: Yeah. So at 15:10 UTC we started seeing a tail in our payment enrichment path. Latency on the validation microservice spiked from median ~20ms to p99 4.3s for about ~18 minutes. The spike coincided with several cache flushes — we think due to... uh, leaders rebalancing? There's a flurry of K-V cache misses and downstream batching grew because more requests hit disk-backed model variants. We'll put the timeline in the doc.
[00:02:10] Jordan: And to add, the fallback didn't kick in consistently. Some requests retried which piled on, creating a small feedback loop.

[00:03:05] Samir Patel: On Redwood's side we pulled the runtime traces. We saw a burst of cache invalidations roughly at 15:08 which aligns. The interesting bit — and this is perhaps mis-phrased — the cache TTL configs were low for certain keys and combined with our steady-state prefix caching, you get cache thundering under heavy re-requests. Also, we observed batching windows elongated because several requests lacked KV-context and were forced to rebuild the KV cache; that increases per-token time.
[00:04:00] Marcus Holt: Yeah, and one weirdness — a handful of requests routed to a quantized variant that had slightly different attention implementation. Those were slower under certain sequence lengths.

[00:05:12] Priya Singh: From security — we want to confirm that no customer data was exfiltrated, especially during the disk fallback. Can you confirm the access pattern?
[00:05:24] Samir Patel: To our knowledge, no data left the VPC. The disk fallback is still inside your private subnet for the Dedicated config we used. However, because some requests ended up on older model artifacts, audit logs need to be double-checked. We'll include the request ids in the export.

[00:06:40] Avery Chen: Quick clarification: MatrixPay is running a hybrid route right now — primary hosted region us-west and backup Dedicated Pool in eu-west, correct?
[00:06:52] Ibrahim Khan: Correct. Primary is hosted for most traffic but we have reserved capacity for peak bursts. The switch isn't transparent enough though; we saw cross-region routing add like 200ms sometimes.

[00:08:00] Samir Patel: We also want to flag that the smart routing policy at the time had a 'latency tolerant' fallback which prioritized capacity over identical model variant. That meant requests could be routed to a eu-west model with different quantization. We'll share the routing logs.

[00:09:40] Tasha Reed: From product POV, our success criteria are: p99 < 500ms for payment validation, <1% error rate. That was violated yesterday. So we're sensitive to any mitigation that risks precision.

[00:10:15] Marcus Holt: We attached three example traces in the incident doc. Two of them show repeated cache rebuilds within 300ms windows.

[00:11:05] Samir Patel: The mitigation surface we proposed internally — temporary: raise TTL for the hot keys, enforce stricter routing to keep the same quantization variant for active customers, and add a short circuit fallback earlier (like a cached response or static heuristic) to avoid rebuild storms. Longer term: we recommend adding an autoscaler that considers KV miss rate as a signal and a rewrite of the fallback policy to decouple model variant from capacity fallback.

[00:12:40] Lena Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. Two quick asks: 1) can you provide a small benchmark that shows the accuracy delta between the quantized variant and baseline? We need to see tradeoff numbers, not just latencies. 2) We need to make sure the rollback path is safe for the payments path — i.e. not introduce silent degradation.

[00:13:25] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We have a micro-benchmark where we run a curated prompt set and measure token-level divergence + latency. We'll attach the CSV. Note there can be transcription in the names — the benchmark includes 3k prompts representative of your validation calls.

[00:14:10] Jordan: There's one more thing — the ops runbook didn't capture the combined TTL and routing mismatch. We ended up doing manual fix which is not great.

[00:15:14] Nora Liu: Nora here — I'll take ownership of updating the runbook. Samir, can you send a suggested doc diff?
[00:15:22] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll draft a small runbook diff: detection thresholds, immediate mitigations (raise TTL, pin model variant), and when to invoke full rollback to previous model.

[00:16:40] Priya Singh: Security also wants to confirm key management — when caching is rebuilt from disk does any KMS interaction happen? We need to confirm that KMS/HSM calls are idempotent and audited.
[00:16:55] Samir Patel: KMS calls only happen during initial boot for key unwrap. The cache rebuild merely reads encrypted artifacts from the storage layer; we log KMS unwrap events. We'll pull the unwrap logs for the window.

[00:18:05] Marcus Holt: A question for Redwood product — is there an out-of-box guard to prevent a capacity fallback from selecting a different model family? We thought the platform would keep the same architecture for production customers.
[00:18:22] Avery Chen: Good callout. The current policy has a compatibility-first mode but not always enforced. We can propose a stricter 'variant affinity' policy for your account, effectively disallowing model-family switches during fallback. That requires a config change and agreement from both sides about available variants.

[00:19:50] Ibrahim Khan: That would help. Also, what's the impact on cost and latency if we force variant affinity vs allowing cheaper fallbacks? We need those numbers for finance.

[00:20:10] Samir Patel: If you pin affinity to the same variant, you'll lose some of the cost-upside during capacity events because we can't route to cheaper quantized variants. Latency will be more stable but cost per-token could increase 6-12% under some traffic patterns. We'll quantify for your 24-72h window.

[00:21:40] Tasha Reed: Tradeoff accepted if it keeps p99 within target. For larger events we can discuss a staged policy.

[00:22:30] Marcus Holt: On the telemetry side — we need per-token and per-request IDs surfaced to our traces. Right now we get aggregated metrics but not the token-level timeline. We want a short-term export of the raw traces for the outage window.

[00:23:05] Samir Patel: We'll export the traces and the KV hit/miss timelines. Note that the export might have some PII redaction — we'll include request ids tied to your internal ids so you can match.

[00:24:40] Priya Singh: Also please include the audit log slices for model artifact load and KMS unwraps.

[00:25:35] Avery Chen: Let's talk mitigation plan concretely: 1) Immediate (next 24h): raise TTL for hot keys, enable variant-affinity policy for MatrixPay, and roll out a temporary circuit that returns a cached heuristic for extreme tail cases. 2) Short-term (week): run a 10% canary pinned to Dedicated pool with stricter telemetry and compare p50/p95/p99 72h. 3) Medium-term: add KV-miss-based autoscaling signal and change fallback policy to prefer same-model variant or graceful degrade with static output. Does that match what folks want?

[00:26:20] Lena Ortiz: Yes that's aligned. We need clear numbers for step 2 though — what does success look like for the canary?

[00:26:40] Samir Patel: Success: p99 < 500ms and token-level divergence < 0.5% on the curated validation suite, and no elevated error rate. We'll produce bench numbers.

[00:27:55] Tasha Reed: Also we want a rollback plan for the canary — if p99 goes above 700ms we automatically stop canary.

[00:28:10] Nora Liu: Adding that to next steps.

[00:29:05] Marcus Holt: I want to call out a peculiar trace where two requests collided rebuilding the KV cache and then each retried creating a mini storm. Could we rate limit rebuilds? Like a single-flight for cache rebuild keyed by user token?

[00:29:40] Samir Patel: Yes single-flight is possible — we have a prototype single-flight gate for prefix rebuilds. It reduces duplicate rebuilds at the cost of slight extra latency for the first caller. That's probably a net win during storms. We'll include the patch in the runbook diff.

[00:31:00] Priya Singh: On the compliance front — our legal asks for a statement that no data was exported and a timeline of any KMS unwrapping. We'll need that doc for audit.

[00:31:20] Avery Chen: We'll produce that statement and the unwrap timeline.

[00:32:15] Ibrahim Khan: A practical question: if we move to Private deployment entirely (on-prem/VPC), would this eliminate cross-region routing issues?

[00:32:30] Samir Patel: Private deployment removes cross-region variability but introduces ops overhead. You'll get lower network variance but you'd be responsible for scaling and patching. We can support a managed Private option where Redwood handles the runtime patching with a private control plane. Priya, that also meets a lot of your SOC2 needs.

[00:33:45] Priya Singh: We'd prefer a managed Private if the compliance overhead is lower. Please send the SOC2 mapping and the support SLA.

[00:34:12] Samir Patel: We'll send the security checklist and SOC2 scope.

[00:35:00] Lena Ortiz: Quick note on communication — we'd like a 6-hour update during mitigations pinned to an incident channel.

[00:35:08] Nora Liu: We'll coordinate and make sure channel invites go out.

[00:36:20] Tasha Reed: Are there any longer-term architectural changes Redwood is planning that would reduce this class of failures?

[00:36:35] Samir Patel: Yes, we're working on a model-variant affinity control, KV-miss autoscaling, and a more deterministic fallback that returns structured fallbacks instead of opaque model variants. Timeline for those features is Q3 roadmap items; we can prioritize some for MatrixPay as a customer request.

[00:37:55] Marcus Holt: Can we get an estimate of effort to implement single-flight rebuild, TTL changes, and variant-affinity? We need to plan on-call coverage.

[00:38:15] Samir Patel: Single-flight: small runtime patch (1-2 engineer-weeks), TTL config change: immediate, variant-affinity policy: config + small control-plane change (2-3 engineer-weeks if prioritized). We'll ask product to fast-track.

[00:39:50] Avery Chen: Let's capture owners. Samir will produce bench + runbook diff; Nora will update runbook and open support case; Marcus will export traces; Priya will confirm security checklist; Lena and Tasha will sign off on canary acceptance criteria.

[00:40:30] Jordan: Small nit — we saw some misattributed speaker labels in the transcript earlier which threw off the first timeline. Future exports please add participant email mapping to speaker ids.

[00:41:05] Nora Liu: Good note, we'll include email mappings.

[00:42:10] Avery Chen: Any other questions?
[00:42:18] Lena Ortiz: One last ask — could Redwood run an injected-storm test in a non-prod environment to exercise the fallback paths before we do canary?

[00:42:35] Samir Patel: Yes — we can schedule an injected test with controlled cache churn and watch behavior. It would be best scheduled before we flip traffic to canary.

[00:43:20] Marcus Holt: Great. Let's aim to run the injection on 2026-06-27.

[00:44:05] Avery Chen: Ok I'll send invites and the action item list. Any final comments?
[00:44:20] Priya Singh: Please make sure the SOC2 mapping includes encryption-in-transit + key rotation cadence.

[00:44:40] Samir Patel: Noted.

[00:45:12] Nora Liu: I'll summarize and share the meeting notes within 24h.

[00:46:00] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the bench and traces are shared.
[00:46:10] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, talk soon.

[00:47:00] Meeting closed.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker identification occasionally generic, some product names mis-transcribed (e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood dedicate), and technical terms (KV cache) sometimes split as K-V cash.
